newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan names first ventures to join OTC 2nd section.
newsitem.headline: Japan names first ventures to join OTC 2nd section.

text.p: More than a year after it was established, a special section of Tokyo's over-the-counter (OTC) share market on Wednesday finally signed up its first two members.

The Japan Securities Dealers Association (JSDA) announced that two small venture companies -- ATL Systems Inc and A&Cmos Inc -- will be allowed to register their shares on the OTC second section next month.
The section was set up in July 1995 to make it easier for start-up companies to raise funds. Such high-risk ventures have had problems issuing shares due to a lack of steady profits.
The establishment of the OTC second section was aimed at research-oriented and high-tech ventures but has clearly been less than a roaring success.
ATL Systems, a software developer and manufacturer, plans to register 1,100 shares through a public offering on the second section on December 17.
The company, which has capital totalling 120 million yen ($1.08 million) and six employees, suffered a current loss of 26.4 million yen ($237,000) for the full year to April 1996.
A Tokyo-based integrated circuits developer and maker, A&Cmos plans to register 3,000 shares on the second section through a public offering on December 25.
The company, capitalised at 160 million yen ($1.44 million) and with six employees, also suffered a current loss of 36.2 million yen ($326,000) for the full business year to July.

Venture firms have been unable to register shares on the second section because securities houses, as lead managers for such issues, have been cautious in screening candidates in case they post big losses after going public.
But recent studies show that new venture companies are keen to go public.
According to a survey of 1,081 independent venture companies, about 85 percent of the firms created since 1990 want to go public. (1$=111 yen)
